candidate_instruction_lines.text: For foreground layers recovered from flattened artwork, derive coverage from guide-identified stems and attached object contours, not shared pigments or guide rectangles. Solid interiors occlude; genuine negative spaces remain transparent; internal veins are not holes. Preserve original boundary pixels and restore source scene pixels only within verified foreground coverage. Closing and flood-fill can bridge real gaps: verify their result against local contours rather than assuming connected regions are foreground.

Before batch rendering, test a difficult crossing using aligned source, transformed unoccluded sprite and composite crops, with a thin mask-boundary overlay. Check neighboring frames and both sides of the boundary: original detail must remain visible through genuine gaps and disappear within solid occluders, respecting the requested layer order. These are internal diagnostics, not added deliverables. A filled mask preview or favorable sampled review alone is insufficient.

Reserve work for export and delivery. If detail is already missing in a raw frame, repair compositing first; regenerate affected frames, reopen the actual export, verify the repaired crossing and requested dimensions/timing, then deliver that checked file.

likely_mechanism.classification: excess restoration across genuine gaps plus incomplete stem fill
likely_mechanism.inference: The candidate uses broad cream-contour thresholding followed by MaxFilter(3), flood fill and MinFilter(3). The saved mask covers background pixel (330,230), which is unmasked by the passed baseline; its source color is the blue mural field. Both arms paste the same supplied actors at the same indexed motion. Extra restoration across negative spaces is strongly consistent with the observed loss of visible actor patterns. The saved candidate also omits some stem interiors; this is not a pure uniform expansion.
likely_mechanism.boundary: This identifies a saved mask defect and code path consistent with the recorded loss. It does not apportion the delivered MP4 MAE to individual pixels or prove that this one sample caused the full loss.

likely_mechanism.classification: incomplete occluder interiors rather than pigment or actor replacement
likely_mechanism.inference: The candidate flood-fills cream outline pixels after sealing stem endpoints, then adds approximate leaf polygons. The saved mask leaves the inside of the actual source stem transparent at (292,230), while the passed baseline fills it. Candidate mask rows around y220–320 frequently retain only two outline strips across the stem. Both source-actor checks still pass, while rear and front veil crossing checks fail. This is consistent with actors showing through solid occluder interiors.
likely_mechanism.boundary: The stored-mask holes and narrower manual leaf vertices are observed. Their separate contributions to the delivered MP4 error are not measured. The NumPy import failure was recovered using Pillow and is not shown to be the quality cause.

likely_mechanism.classification: baseline restoration bridges a genuine gap; candidate succeeds on this execution
likely_mechanism.inference: The baseline uses MaxFilter(5), outside flood fill and MinFilter(5); its saved mask restores mural background at (330,230). The successful candidate uses outline-local flood fill followed by explicit stem/leaf interiors and leaves that mural point unmasked. Both source-actor failures in the baseline are absent in the candidate.
likely_mechanism.boundary: This demonstrates that the same broad mask failure also occurs in the baseline. Together with the other pairs, it supports an unstable execution mechanism rather than a deterministic causal claim about procedure wording.

completed_regression_snapshot.scope_note: These are regression results only; they are not fresh holdout rates or final acceptance.

cross_case_findings: All six trace-inspected native executions completed delivery with fixed gpt-6.1-sol/low, immutable sources, valid budgets and correct container/timing structure. The two candidate losses concern content compositing.
Every selected artifact received a same-SHA sampled visual pass; independent source/depth checks still detected failures. A favorable sampled review did not establish exact mask fidelity.

The learned candidate text explicitly warns against bridged gaps and hollow interiors and asks for aligned source/sprite/composite crops with a thin boundary overlay. Recorded tool usage does not demonstrate that full diagnostic in either losing candidate.

The two failures have opposite mask defects: excess coverage can erase actor detail; missing solid occluder coverage can preserve actor detail but break depth. Treating either generic flood filling or generic shrinkage as universally correct would be unsupported.
limitations: All four regression pairs were complete; the full cycle was still running. This report makes no final admission, quality gain or heldout-rate claim.
Passed baseline masks are comparison references, not exact semantic ground truth. Pixel-count differences are not a fresh quality score.

Existing saved PNG mask samples, source pixels, native trace code and immutable output hashes were inspected. No delivered video was decoded or rerendered, no grading was rerun, and no encoded-pixel causal effect size is asserted.

This observational single-run comparison cannot establish that procedure wording alone caused the difference. It identifies concrete execution mechanisms and diagnostic steps absent from the recorded calls.
